days.title: Submerged Ports and Imperial Villas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Lacus Baianus
stops.detail: In addition, the remains of the commercial ports of Baia (Lacus Baianus) and the Portus Julius are found submerged on this coast.

stops.name: Pausilypon
stops.detail: Around the first century BC, in fact, the entire coastal area north of Naples was a flourishing health resort, made fashionable also by the presence of an imperial villa, the Pausilypon precisely, which gave its name to the Promontory of Posillipo, built by the wealthy freedman Publius Vedius Pollio.

days.title: Archeological Treasures and Naval History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: ninfeo di Punta Epitaffio
stops.detail: Among the most valuable environments, which today are submerged, there is the nymphaeum of Punta Epitaffio, a triclinium serving as a banquet hall dating back to the era of Emperor Claudius, whose statues have been moved inside the Archaeological Museum of the Phlegraean Fields where the room has been reconstructed.

stops.name: Capo Miseno
stops.detail: Further north was the port of Capo Miseno, the historic seat of the Roman imperial fleet.
